conventions: γάμος and its family take one head policy across the chapter. Where the ASV writes *marriage feast* for the single noun (22:2, 22:3, 22:4, 22:9) the phrase is one unit headed on *marriage*, *feast* being the generic completion under rules 66 and 91; where it writes a bare *wedding* the noun stands alone (22:10), and the attributive genitive γάμου is *wedding* alone (22:11, 22:12). The same test decides the verb: 22:30's γαμίζονται → *are given in marriage* heads on *marriage*, because the corpus spends the γαμ- root on *marry*, *marriage* and *wedding* and never on *give*, and rule 17 forbids choosing *given* merely because it is the English phrase's formal verb head. The ASV's *in* inside that phrase answers to no Greek preposition and stays inside the verb's unit.

ἐπερωτάω: the object the English verb requires but the Greek leaves unexpressed rides inside the verb's unit as a rule 7 helper, headed on the *ask* word under rule 91 — *asked … a question* at 22:35 and 22:41, *ask … questions* at 22:46, and at 22:35 the supplied *him* as well under rule 74's supplied-object contrast rather than `added` under rule 103. 22:23's bare *they asked* is the same analysis with nothing supplied. Do not read *a question* as a light-verb complement to head on: the Greek expresses no second element, so rule 73 is not in question.

Where the ASV recasts a Greek impersonal plus dative experiencer as a personal English verb, the dative is what the supplied English subject pronoun realizes and takes it as its own unit: σοι δοκεῖ → *thinkest thou* gives *thou* to σοι at 22:17, and ὑμῖν δοκεῖ → *think ye* gives *ye* to ὑμῖν at 22:42, the verb standing alone in both. Where the ASV writes no pronoun the dative has nothing to take and is `unrepresented`: 22:16's οὐ μέλει σοι → *carest not* leaves σοι empty, the English verb's inflection carrying the person. Folding σοι into μέλει's unit there remains defensible; a reference comparison reports it as a disagreement.

*together* is decided by whether a Greek preposition stands to answer to it. At 22:10 and 22:41 nothing does, so it realizes the συν- preverb and rides inside the verb's own unit under rule 106. At 22:34 συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό → *gathered themselves together* has one, so rule 106's scope clause hands the pair to rule 94: ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό is one `noncompositional` unit taking *together* headed on the governed word, the article τό is its own `unrepresented` unit under rule 93, and the verb keeps only *gathered themselves*, the reflexive being a rule 7 helper.

A substantival article before a participle is split by what the ASV wrote for the participle, not by the article's own class. Where the ASV renders the participle as a finite relative clause the article keeps only the pronoun under rule 32 — *them* / *that were bidden* at 22:3 and 22:4, *they* / *made light of it* at 22:5, *they* / *that were bidden* at 22:8, *they* / *that say* at 22:23, *that* / *which was spoken* at 22:31. Where the ASV renders it by a plain nominal instead, no relative clause exists for the article to absorb and the determiner is the article's own: 22:11's τοὺς ἀνακειμένους → *the guests* gives *the* to the article and *guests* to the participle, on the line rules 19, 51, 57, 58, 92 and 102 hold throughout — an article that is present takes whatever determiner the ASV writes. Rule 22's closing sentence, read flat, would empty that article; it is scoped here to the relative-clause rendering, and emptying the article and giving *the guests* whole to the participle remains the competing reading.

22:32 carries two projection facts a later reader should not re-derive. The textual unit SBLGNT.MAT.22.32.v021, whose only compatible reading is r01, leaves the projection with two θεός tokens where the ASV writes one *God*; the surplus token is its own `unrepresented` unit under rule 97's mirror clause, which no corpus unit had needed before. Separately, the ASV writes *God* twice in the second clause and italicizes the predicate: θεός is spent on the bare subject *God*, so the italicized *the God* is `added` under rules 5 and 103 with its determiner inside the unit, and the article ὁ is `unrepresented` under rule 23 because the ASV gives the subject no determiner. GAL.3.20's ὁ δὲ μεσίτης ἑνὸς οὐκ ἔστιν → *a mediator is not a mediator of one* is the identical frame; reading the repetition as a discontinuous second realization under rule 15 remains defensible.
report: Checked all 64 candidate groups and read the dump end to end for the splits the table is blind to (the chapter has only two `added` units: 22:32 *the God* and 22:39 *this*). No construction is analysed two ways without an ASV difference licensing it, so there are no patches; six chapter-wide judgments are recorded in the log.

The article-before-participle bucket (ὁ, T→V) is the one that looked like a real split: 22:3, 22:4, 22:5, 22:8, 22:23 and 22:31 give the article a bare pronoun and the participle the relative clause (rule 32), while 22:11 gives it *the* and the participle the noun *guests*. The difference is the ASV's — a finite relative clause in the six, a plain nominal at 22:11 — so it is not a split.

Flagged rather than promoted: rule 22's closing sentence ('Where a participle follows, rule 32 splits this instead: the article keeps only the pronoun') reads on its face as though it emptied the 22:11 article and handed *the guests* to the participle. This chapter read it as scoped to the relative-clause rendering, on the contract's most repeated line — an article that is present takes whatever determiner the ASV writes (rules 19, 51, 57, 58, 92, 102) — and on rule 90's gloss that rule 32's 'and nothing else' limits what the article may absorb rather than denying it a word. I did not amend rule 22: one instance, and no corpus query was run on the shape, which is the weak-rule case the brief warns about. A pass holding LEMMA=ὁ MORPH=T- NEXT=V- STATUS=aligned TARGET='^the$' against the same filters with STATUS=unrepresented can settle it.

*together* is placed two ways and the source licenses it: rule 106 gives it to the συν- preverb at 22:10 and 22:41, but at 22:34 a Greek preposition stands to answer to it, so rule 106's own scope clause hands the pair to rule 94, ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό takes *together* as one `noncompositional` unit and the intervening τό is `unrepresented` under rule 93. Nothing to reconcile.

The γαμ- family is headed one way throughout: *marriage feast* on *marriage* (22:2, 22:3, 22:4, 22:9), bare *wedding* where the ASV writes it (22:10, 22:11, 22:12), and 22:30's *are given in marriage* on *marriage* rather than on the formal English verb *given*. Rule 91's operational test gives the same answer in all four shapes.

22:44's ἕως ἄν → *Till* is the one unit that goes beyond rule 50's two named arms (the modal auxiliary; compression into a *-soever* word). No part of *Till* answers to ἄν, so rule 39's test read alone would push toward `noncompositional`; the joined `aligned` unit rests on rule 50's flat 'ἄν is aligned' and its correction clause. Left as the verse has it — a chapter with more than one instance should settle the status.

BSB: all 17 disagreements are documented convention differences, not errors — rule 20 displacement (22:2 τῷ, 22:8 τοῖς, 22:24 τήν and τῷ, 22:25 τῷ, 22:44 τῷ), rule 23 determinerlessness (22:2 τῶν, 22:13 τῶν, 22:19 τοῦ, 22:20 ἡ, 22:32 ὁ where the ASV writes a bare subject *God*), rule 38 (22:10 οἱ, 22:23 τῇ), rule 36's absorbed εἰς (22:16), rule 72's generalizing ἐάν (22:9, which rule 72 names as not a correction), rule 93's article inside a noncompositional unit (22:34 τό), and 22:16 σοι, where the ASV's *carest* carries the person and writes no separate word. No edge was changed to move the rate.

The two `unrepresented` units a later reader is most likely to query are 22:16 σοι and 22:32's second θεός; both carry verse notes, and the second is the projection's textual surplus, now recorded in the log with its variant unit id.
